Definition: from a compound of G3717 and G4228; to be straight-footed, i.e. (figuratively) to go directly forward:--walk uprightly.
BiblicalUsage: To walk uprightly is to walk straight, and the word appears once, when Paul withstood Peter at Antioch because he saw they walked not uprightly according to the truth of the gospel.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe walking uprightly is not about my posture but about the gospel: Peter's walk bent away from the truth, and Paul called him on it in front of everyone.
